newsitem.title: UK: UK announces proposals for tougher alcohol regime.
newsitem.headline: UK announces proposals for tougher alcohol regime.

text.p: The British government announced proposals on Thursday for a tougher regime surrounding alcohol sales in an attempt to cut teenage drinking.
-- to allow police to confiscate alcohol from those under-18 drinking in public.
-- to make it an offence for adults to buy alcohol in a shop at the request of unsupervised youngsters.
-- to use teenagers, working under the close supervision of "enforcement authorities", to check rogue retailers selling alcohol to under-18s.

Interior minister George Howarth could not give a firm commitment on the timetable for any legislation but said the first measure -- police confiscating alcohol -- is heading for the statute book and will be enforceable by August.
He said the new measures would only succeed with the full co-operation of the drinks retailing industry.

"It is now for the industry to show this can work, in stamping out underage drinking. If these measures fail to curb the problem then the government will take further steps," Howarth told a news conference.
He welcomed the industry-backed Portman Group's new code of practice, launched on Thursday.
